Task: Repair the literal-hash-suffix corruption in MarkdownFile heading titles only. Current source "# C#" produces title "C", and both heading/section lookup by "C#" fail. Within already-recognized ATX lines, only a trailing run of hashes separated from the preceding title by a space or tab is a closing marker. Adjacent hashes remain literal title text. This includes cases followed by trailing whitespace, or followed by an independent closing run. Preserve current trimming, separated-closer behavior, empty title, level, source line number, fence exclusion, hierarchy boundaries, lookup semantics, and exact original content. Markdown remains a narrow raw-text helper: no inline escape decoding, no full CommonMark parser, no new indentation/opening grammar, no source-fidelity redesign. Only existing approved model files may be modified.

Baseline pattern: r"^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)[ \t]*#*[ \t]*$"

Candidate pattern: r"^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)(?:(?<=[ \t])#+)?[ \t]*$"

Let me think about the semantics of the new regex.

The new pattern: after marker and required separator [ \t]+, then text (lazy), then an optional group that requires a hash run immediately preceded by a space or tab (lookbehind (?<=[ \t])#+), then trailing [ \t]*$.

Let me consider the test cases:

1. "# C#": marker #, separator " ", then text ".*?" lazy, then optional closer, then [ \t]*$. For the overall match to succeed: the line is "# C#". After marker+separator, remaining is "C#". The text group must consume something, and the closer is optional. Try text = "C#": then the closer is empty, [ \t]* matches "", $. Match succeeds with text = "C#". Since the regex engine is lazy on text, first tries text = "", then closer (?:(?<=[ \t])#+)? — at position after " " (separator consumed " "), the position is at "C#". Lookbehind checks that the previous character is a space/tab — yes (the separator space). So closer can match "#"? Wait, closer is #+ — at position "C#", the next character is "C" not "#", so #+ fails at this position. Actually the closer group is optional, so it can also match empty. Then [ \t]*$ — at position "C#", [ \t]* matches "", then $ fails because "C#" remains. Backtrack: text = "C", position is at "#". Closer: lookbehind — the previous character is "C" (not space/tab), so (?<=[ \t])#+ fails; the group can match empty. Then [ \t]*$ fails at "#". Backtrack: text = "C#", position is at end. Closer is empty, [ \t]*$, $ succeeds. So text = "C#". Title "C#". ✓ (matches observed)

2. "# C# #": line = "# C# #". After marker+separator (greedy [ \t]+ consumes " ", one space), remaining is "C# #". text is lazy: tries "" → position "C# #". Closer: lookbehind previous char is space → #+ needs to start with # but next char is "C" → fails; empty ok. [ \t]*$ fails. text = "C" → position "# #". Closer: previous char "C" is not a space → fails. [ \t]*$ fails. text = "C#" → position " #". Closer: lookbehind previous char "#" is not space/tab → fails. [ \t]*$ fails (" " is whitespace but then "#" is not). Wait [ \t]*$ — at position " #", [ \t]* matches " ", then $ fails at "#". Backtrack [ \t]* to match "", $ fails at " ". text = "C# " → position "#". Closer: lookbehind previous char is space → #+ matches "#", position at end. [ \t]*$, $ succeeds. So text = "C# " → after .strip() → "C#". ✓ (matches observed "C#")

Hmm interesting. So "# C# #" gives text = "C# " and strips to "C#". Correct per spec: adjacent hashes are literal, separated trailing closing run is a marker. ✓

3. "# Title #": text = "Title " and closer "#" → "Title". ✓

4. "# ##": line = "# ##". After marker+separator, remaining is "##". text = "" → position "##". Closer: lookbehind previous char is space → #+ matches "##", position at end. [ \t]*$ succeeds. So text = "" → title "". ✓ (matches observed)

But wait — subtle point: for "# ##", is the title "##" (literal) or "" (closing)? Per spec: "Within already-recognized ATX lines, only a trailing run of hashes separated from the preceding title by a space or tab is a closing marker." In "# ##" there is no title preceding the hashes (empty title). The hashes are separated from the preceding (empty) title by the required separator space. The spec says "adjacent hashes remain literal title text. This includes cases followed by trailing whitespace, or followed by an independent closing run." And "preserve current trimming, separated-closer behavior, empty title, ...".

In the baseline, "# ##" → baseline pattern: text lazy, [ \t]*#*[ \t]*$. text = "" → position "##", [ \t]* matches "", #* matches "##", [ \t]*$, $ succeeds. So baseline also gives empty title for "# ##". So the candidate matches baseline behavior on this case. And the public check expects "" for "# ##", and it passed.

Now, the question the prompt asks me to investigate: "Is a separated closing run after an adjacent hash mishandled?"

Hmm, "a separated closing run after an adjacent hash" — that's case 2: "# C# #". We verified the candidate produces "C#" — correct per spec. Adjacent hashes "C#" literal, then " #" separated closing run stripped.

Spec: title is "Title", then trailing run "# #"? Hmm, "only a trailing run of hashes separated from the preceding title by a space or tab is a closing marker". So for "Title # #", the trailing run is... the last run is "#", preceded by " #". Hmm. What does the baseline do?

For "# Title # #": after marker+sep, "Title # #". text lazy: tries "" → [ \t]*#*[ \t]*$ fails. ... text = "Title" → position " # #". [ \t]* matches " ", #* matches "#", [ \t]* matches " ", $ fails at "#". text = "Title " → position "# #": [ \t]* matches "", #* matches "#", [ \t]* matches " ", $ fails. text = "Title # " → position "#": #* matches "#", [ \t]*, $ succeeds. So baseline text = "Title # " → strip → "Title #".

Candidate for "# Title # #": after marker+sep, "Title # #". text lazy: "" → closer at position "Title..." — lookbehind is space (separator) → #+ fails (next is "T"). Empty closer, [ \t]*$ fails. text = "Title" → position " # #": closer: lookbehind space → #+ matches "#", position " #". [ \t]* matches " ", $ fails at "#". Hmm wait — after closer consumed "#", position is at " #". [ \t]* matches " ", then $ fails. Backtrack: closer #+ can match fewer... #+ is just "#" here. Backtrack to text = "Title " → position "# #": closer: lookbehind previous char is space → #+ matches "#", position " #". [ \t]* " ", $ fails. Backtrack: closer empty (lookbehind ok but #+ needs at least one; #+ matches "#", tried). Hmm wait, at text = "Title " (with trailing space), position is "# #". Closer: lookbehind previous char (the space in "Title ") is space → #+ matches first "#", position " #". [ \t]* matches " ", $ fails. Backtrack [ \t]* to "" → $ fails at " ". So closer fails → group empty → [ \t]*$ fails at "#". Backtrack to text = "Title # " → position "#": closer: lookbehind previous char is space → #+ matches "#", position end. [ \t]*$ succeeds. So text = "Title # " → strip → "Title #". Same as baseline. ✓
